slides.title: Relationship questions you'd never say out loud

slides.q: How do I tell my partner I want to try something new in bed?
slides.a: Bring it up outside the bedroom, at a relaxed time. Frame it as excitement, not criticism, like "I've been curious about trying something, what do you think?" Ask what they're curious about too. If they're not into it, take that well. A good conversation is the goal, and both of you should feel free to say no.

slides.q: Is it a red flag if my partner's ex still texts them?
slides.a: Not automatically. Some exes stay friends, co-parent, or share a friend group. What matters is how often, what it's about, and whether your partner is open about it. If it's secretive or makes you feel pushed aside, say so calmly. How they respond when you bring it up tells you more than the texts themselves.

slides.q: How do we split bills when one of us earns way more?
slides.a: A lot of couples split shared costs by income instead of 50/50. If one of you earns 60% of your combined income, they cover 60% of rent and bills. Others pool everything or keep a joint account just for shared stuff. The best system is the one you both agree feels fair. Revisit it when incomes change.

slides.q: Is it normal to not like how my partner kisses?
slides.a: More common than you'd think. Everyone kisses differently, and styles can take time to sync up. Instead of critiquing, show them what you like and say something positive when they do it, like "I love when you do that." Most people are glad to adjust. Being gentle about it keeps it fun instead of awkward.

slides.q: Is it weird to still use my ex's Netflix?
slides.a: A little. It keeps a small tie to them, they can see what you watch, and they can kick you off anytime. Streaming services also limit sharing outside one household. If you're trying to move on, logging out is a clean small step. Treat yourself to your own account, or cancel and enjoy the quiet.
